title: Release Day Pocket Manual & Signal Timeline — May 2026 (Draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, day-of release pocket manual and signal timeline for the May 2026 infra + serving runtime push. Meant for on-call leads, release shepherds, and pair-run engineers. Keep this open during the window; treat it as the single source of quick decisions. Longer runbook links are in linked_artifacts.

High-level objective:
- Deploy runtime v2.8.1 with KV cache improvement and batching heuristics turned on for low-latency workloads.
- Keep end-to-end latency P95 <= 120ms and error rate < 0.3% across hosted tier.
- Complete staged canary and 30% traffic ramp within the maintenance window.

Quick contact list:
- Release owner / shepherd: Ava Chen (pager: ava.redwood, slack: @ava)
- Lead SRE: Marcus Patel (pager: marcus.redwood)
- Serving runtime lead: Lena Ortiz (slack: @lena)
- Rollback owner: Ravi Shah
- Observability/telemetry: Claire Ng
- Escalation path: oncall -> SRE lead -> Eng manager -> Eng director

Day-of timeline (all times UTC) — compressed, pocket view:
- T-60m (09:00): Final preflight check (see PRECHECKs). Notify #release-day-ops: "green" or list blockers.
- T-30m (09:30): Freeze deploy window, disable non-essential scheduled jobs that generate load (jobs tagged offline-release).
- T-15m (09:45): Canary cohort booted (3 instances across us-west1/us-east1/eu-west1). Run basic smoke suite.
- T+0 (10:00): Begin canary traffic routing (1% traffic). Monitor 15m rolling window metrics.
- T+15m (10:15): If metrics OK, escalate to 5% traffic. If any critical signal, abort and rollback to v2.8.0.
- T+45m (10:45): Ramp to 30% traffic. Begin automated slow-roll checks and quality evals against golden prompt set.
- T+90m (11:30): Ramp to 60% (if previous holds). Start scheduled migration of routing weights in config store.
- T+120m (12:00): Full rollout (100%) if all SLOs satisfied for preceding windows. Post-rollout telemetry collection for 2 hours.

Preflight checklist (T-60m):
- [ ] All blocking Jira tickets for this release are closed (INF-2987, INF-3001)
- [ ] DB schema migration plan reviewed (none for this release)
- [ ] Backplane config pinned and validated in staging -> prod config store
- [ ] Canary images built and signed: serving-runtime:v2.8.1-rc3
- [ ] Grafana dashboards loaded and default refresh set to 15s for the window (latency, errors, capacity)
- [ ] Alerting silences set for non-critical noise (list silences in Slack)
- [ ] Pager rota confirmed, primary/secondary tagged in #release-day-ops
- [ ] Runbook snippets available: smoke-tests, rollback commands, traffic-weight script

Smoke tests (run on each canary region):
- Basic generation health check: send 10 short prompts (S0..S9) — expect no 5xxs and mean latency < 200ms
- KV-cache spot check: repeated prefix scenario for 20 tokens — ensure cache hit ratio increases
- Tokenization regressions: verify sample text encodes/decodes without mismatch
- Streaming boundary test: open streaming socket and send 50 incremental tokens; ensure stream commits without gap
- Auth/tenant isolation: sample tenant token must not access another tenant's trace logs

Acceptance signals (pass -> continue, fail -> pause & investigate):
- Latency P95 (hosted tier) change from baseline <= +15ms
- Error rate (5xx) absolute < 0.3% and relative increase < 50% over baseline
- CPU/GPU utilization within expected envelope (no immediate OOM or queue stall signs)
- Memory growth (per-process) flat over 30m window
- Golden prompt diffs: BLEU-like quality metrics show no regressions on curated prompts

Abort / rollback criteria (immediate):
- Any data corruption or misrouting of tenant requests
- Error rate spikes > 1% sustained over 5 minutes
- P99 latency > 1s for > 10m in two or more regions
- Canary control-plane reprovision failures > 2 in 15m

Rollback quick steps (pocket commands):
- Revert traffic weights to previous tag: ./scripts/route-weights --set stable:v2.8.0
- Trigger restart of canary pool: infractl restart --pool serving-canary --tag stable:v2.8.0
- Post-rollback verification: run minimal smoke-suite and confirm error rate returned to baseline
- Fill incident channel with short summary and tag oncall/sre

Observability checklist (during windows):
- Monitor these dashboards (open links in browser):
  - serving/latency-p95-p99 (compare to 24h baseline)
  - serving/errors-by-type (drill into 5xxs and grpc codes)
  - infra/gpu-queue-depth (watch for queuing and hot-spots)
  - model/quality-regressions (golden prompt diffs)
- Enhance traces for first 100 requests: set DEBUG_TRACE=1 for a small cohort
- Export a roll log: ./telemetry/export-roll-log --window "2026-05-04T09:30Z/2026-05-04T12:30Z" --name may-release-v2.8.1

Release notes (user-facing draft) — top of release:
Title: Serving runtime v2.8.1 — faster KV cache and smarter batching
Summary (one-liner): Improved prefix cache behavior reduces token-level latency for common conversation patterns; batching heuristics reduce per-token compute for large concurrent fanout.
What changed (high level):
- KV cache improvement: better locality scoring and adaptive TTLs for hot prefixes. Expected 8–15% P95 latency improvement on multi-turn chat patterns.
- Batching heuristics: dynamic batch sizing for mixed short/long prompt workloads (fewer token stalls).
- Minor bugfixes: streaming reconnection path, tokenization edge-case fix for emoji sequences.
Impact and compatibility:
- No API changes. Clients should see lower latency for repeated prefixes. No model signature changes.
Known issues (to surface):
- Rarely, under specific mixed tenant bursts, KV cache warm-up may cause a short P99 bump for ~2–3 minutes during first customer traffic (we are tracking INF-3052)
- Small chance of higher memory footprint during very high concurrency; SRE will autoscale X instances as needed

Developer notes (internal):
- Build: CI artifact ID: serving-runtime:v2.8.1-rc3 (promote to release tag on success)
- Infra: requires a config-store rollout to include new routing knobs; see PR #612 linked above
- QA: regression harness updated (golden set v2026-05-01) — run locally with ./qa/regression --golden v2026-05-01

Post-release tasks (owners):
- Day+0 (Ava): Confirm 2h post-roll telemetry snapshot and post to #release-summary
- Day+1 (Claire): Run full golden prompt quality suite and open regression tickets if divergent
- Day+3 (Lena): Sweep for streaming edge-case reports; collect customer traces for any anomalies
- Day+7 (Marcus): Retro + incident drill if rollback was triggered; create follow-ups for automation gaps

Open questions / TODO (live):
- QA: Do we need a separate slow-path canary for high-context long-sequence jobs? (Lena to advise)
- Automation: Should ramp steps be automated in infractl? (Marcus to sketch)
- Observability: Add an ephemeral synthetic that mimics the largest-tenant multi-turn pattern (Claire)

Quick access commands (for console):
- Check canary versions: infractl list --pool serving-canary --format short
- Set traffic weights: infractl route-set --pool serving --weights v2.8.1=0.01,v2.8.0=0.99
- Revert to stable: infractl rollback --pool serving --tag v2.8.0 --confirm

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep notes chronological in incident thread. Short timestamps, short bullets.
- If we see a subtle quality regression during 30% ramp, do NOT continue to 60% even if latency looks fine. Quality trumps latency for customer trust.

Attachment: draft release notes above can be copy-pasted to documentation repo and to the customer changelog. Use simple language and link to the technical appendix for interested partners.

-- end pocket manual --
